layers.note: A herb of prairies, meadows, rocky balds and open ground.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 2,000 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −30 °C, gone by −40 °C, up to about 16 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −50 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −60 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 7 to 28 °C; gone below 4 °C, where summers are too short, and above 32 °C.

degree_days_0.note: Across its range, about 600 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 300.

degree_days_5.note: Across its range, about 200 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 50.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.3, gone by 0.2.

summer_rain.note: No limit: it grows under summer-dry and summer-wet climates alike.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Common yarrow is circumboreal, from sea level to above the tree line (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
